I love it, I love the philosophy behind it, it's made for car nerds by car nerds.

So why do I not recommend it?

I gotta be honest, you really can't tell this game has been in development for over 10 years. Playing BeamNG means a constant barrage of technical issues, textures refusing to load, "no texture", texture corruption, inconstant performance, constant stutters, constant FPS drops, and even when you manage to run the game properly, even when you're not having any issues, it's impossible to justify how heavy it is. Being CPU heavy because of physics simulation is one thing, but why is 8gb of VRAM necessary to run this game properly? How am I constantly running out of VRAM when I have 4gb over the recommended? Why is it so GPU intensive, when the graphics are good at best and the textures are so simple, to say the least?

So, unless you're fine with having to fix some new problem that started out of nowhere every other day, I'd suggest you don't bother, instead of porting it to PS5 they should deal with all the issues the PC version still has after over 10 years in development.

After 250 hours of gameplay, I can confidently say BeamNG.drive is the most fun I’ve ever had destroying things on purpose. This game is basically a physics playground where every crash feels like it was handcrafted by the universe to make you smile.

The soft‑body physics are insane — you can nudge a bumper and watch your entire car fold like a Primark deckchair. And somehow, that’s exactly why it’s brilliant. Every vehicle handles differently, every crash is unique, and every “I wonder what happens if I do this…” turns into a 20‑minute science experiment.

Performance is solid, modding is endless, and the community has created enough content to keep you busy until the heat death of the universe. Whether you’re drifting, rallying, roleplaying, or launching a bus off a cliff at Mach 3, the game never stops being stupidly fun.

10/10 — Highly recommended.
If loving this game is wrong, I don’t want to be right.
